extended changelog: external save-state files (2.20), Altirra.ini portable mode (2.20), portable/registry GUI toggle (3.20)
official package; Altirra.chm 4.40 help (portable mode, Firmware dialog, disk write modes, host device)

paths.path: Inside the Wine prefix: default mode keeps all settings (including input maps) in the Windows registry, which Wine materializes in the prefix (HKCU-backed values in <prefix>/user.reg); portable mode instead uses Altirra.ini next to Altirra64.exe in the install directory. Altirra's public help/changelog documents mapping through Options > Input but does not document a stable serialized controller-binding key/value syntax; edit through the GUI or preserve the release-specific registry/INI data rather than guessing keys.
evidence: docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Portable mode — "Altirra stores settings in an .ini file instead of in the Windows Registry"; enabled via /portable, by creating Altirra.ini directly, or the Options portable/registry toggle

docs:altirra-morechanges.html v2.20 "Non-ASCII characters are now saved correctly into the Altirra.ini file in portable mode"; v2.60 /portablealt:<file>; v3.20 GUI option for switching between portable and registry mode
docs:www.dosgamers.com Altirra guide — "Create an empty file called Altirra.ini in the Altirra folder ... Otherwise settings will be stored in windows registry"
install:sources/emulator-install-sources.json — Altirra/linux is a direct Wine install of the official zip (downloads/Altirra-*.zip, Altirra64.exe, runtime wine)

paths.path: In place inside the game's own emulated media: writes go into the mounted disk/tape images (ATR/ATX/DCM/PRO/XFD/SAP disks, CAS cassettes) under the drive's write mode; the optional H: host device (System > Devices) exposes a host folder for CIO file saves
paths.naming: No sidecar save files: Atari 8-bit titles save to disk/tape, so saves live inside the game image itself (e.g. game.atr); R/W mode writes back to the source image, VRW/VRWSafe (Altirra default) keeps changes in memory until per-drive Save
evidence: docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Using emulated disk images, Write modes — Read/write (R/W) "changes written back to the source image"; Virtual read/write (VRW) "changes are kept in memory without automatically writing them back"; "Altirra defaults to" VRWSafe
docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Host device — the H: device lets CIO programs "access files directly on the host file system"
docs:altirra.html — supported image formats "ATR, ATX, ATZ, DCM, XFD, PRO, ARC, BAS, ROM, BIN, A52, CAS, SAP"

paths.path: User-chosen via File > Save State; Altirra has no fixed per-user states directory (default dialog location follows the last used folder)
paths.naming: *.atstate2 since 3.90 (v2 format, JSON payload inside a zip); legacy *.atstate from 2.20-3.89; quick save/quick load are in-memory only and are lost on exit
evidence: docs:altirra.html changelog 3.90 — "Save state format rewritten to v2 (*.atstate2), now based on JSON within a .zip file"
docs:altirra-morechanges.html v2.20 — "Initial support for external save state files"
docs:forums.atariage.com "Altirra - How to save full state" — "Quick Load/Save State is the same as Load/Save State, just saving to an in-memory save instead of a file"

paths.path: Atari 8-bit OS ROM images hooked up through the Firmware Images dialog (Options > Firmware, with a Scan... button for a ROM folder); external ROMs use the standard Atari 8-bit emulator filenames, with built-in AltirraOS/Altirra BASIC as the no-firmware fallback
paths.naming: Standard external names include ATARIXL.ROM, ATARIOSB.ROM, ATARIBAS.ROM, and 5200.ROM; built-in AltirraOS/Altirra BASIC are fallback firmware. Upstream does not publish canonical checksums for these user firmware files.
evidence: docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Options: Firmware — OS submenu lists built-in firmware plus "any additional firmware image files hooked up to the emulator through the Firmware Images dialog"; Xformer OS-B is "usually named ATARIOSB.ROM"
docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 — recognized ROM filenames include ATARIXL.ROM, ATARIOSB.ROM, ATARIBAS.ROM, 5200.ROM

docs:altirra.html — Altirra "uses the same format and filenames as most other popular Atari 8-bit system emulators" and ships "reimplemented versions of OS, BASIC, and handler ROMs ... without needing Atari ROMs"

linux.notes: Lunchbox installs the canonical Windows Altirra build under Wine (sources/emulator-install-sources.json); keep the portable Altirra.ini (or /portable) inside the install dir for deterministic per-install config, and keep game images writable for in-image saves. AltirraQt (benwbooth/altirraqt AppImage) is a separate Lunchbox emulator target and is deliberately not captured by this record. Verified macos: canonical Altirra has no official macOS or Linux build — the official page distributes Windows binaries only; the unofficial AltirraSDL fork (ilmenit/AltirraSDL, ini at ~/.config/altirra/settings.ini) targets Linux/macOS but is a distinct emulator.

paths.path: Windows Registry (default mode; the exact HKCU key path is not publicly documented and has moved between releases) — or, in portable mode, Altirra.ini in the same directory as Altirra64.exe, selected by /portable, an existing Altirra.ini file, the /portablealt:<file> switch, or the Options portable/registry toggle. Altirra's public help/changelog documents mapping through Options > Input but provides no stable serialized controller-binding key/value syntax; use the GUI or preserve release-specific registry/INI data.
evidence: docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Portable mode — "In portable mode, Altirra stores settings in an .ini file instead of in the Windows Registry"; "Altirra automatically switches to portable mode whenever the INI file is present"
docs:www.dosgamers.com Altirra guide — settings go to the registry unless Altirra.ini exists in the Altirra folder
docs:altirra-morechanges.html v3.20 — "Added a GUI option in settings for switching between portable and registry mode"

paths.path: In place inside the mounted disk/tape images (game's own ATR/ATX/DCM/PRO/XFD/SAP/CAS file); optional H: host device maps a host folder for direct CIO file saves
paths.naming: No sidecar save files; saves are sectors/files inside the game image, subject to the drive write mode (R/W writes back, VRWSafe default buffers until per-drive Save)
evidence: docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 disk Write modes — R/W writes back to source image; VRW/VRWSafe keep changes in memory until Save
docs:Altirra.chm 4.40 Host device — H: device for host filesystem access from CIO programs

paths.path: File > Save State writes to a user-chosen location; no fixed states directory
paths.naming: *.atstate2 (v2, JSON inside zip, since 3.90); legacy *.atstate; quick saves are in-memory only
evidence: docs:altirra.html changelog 3.90 — "*.atstate2" v2 format
docs:altirra-morechanges.html v2.20 — initial support for external save state files

windows.notes: Windows is Altirra's native platform; every Linux/Wine behavior in this record is the same Windows binary observed through the prefix.

linux-flatpak.reason: The official Altirra distribution documents Windows binaries only; no trustworthy upstream Flatpak package is identified.
evidence: docs:https://www.virtualdub.org/altirra.html — official downloads and supported distribution are Windows binaries; no upstream Flatpak is documented

macos.reason: The canonical Altirra project distributes a Windows binary and does not support macOS; unofficial ports are distinct projects.
evidence: docs:https://www.virtualdub.org/altirra.html — official Altirra downloads are Windows executables and no macOS build is listed
